title: Negation of decimals rounds to 34 significant digits, half to even (SP-1)
verdict: `-x`, and `abs(x)` of a negative `x`, past 34 digits: rounded half to even, or a raise at 10³⁸ - 1
description: `-x` of a decimal with more than 34 significant digits rounds it to 34 digits, half to even, in both modes and on both paths: `-12345678901234567890123456789012345678` (a `DECIMAL(38,0)`) gives -12345678901234567890123456789012350000, and `-88926501604876820962013312199159205000` gives 88926501604876820962013312199159200000 (a tie, to the even digit). `abs(x)` returns a positive `x` unchanged and negates a negative one, so it rounds only those. At 10³⁸ - 1 the rounding reaches 10³⁸, which does not fit, so `-x` raises `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` even with ANSI off.

`0 - x` is exact where its type keeps the scale: an `INT` 0 is `DECIMAL(10,0)`, so `0 - x` of a `DECIMAL(38,s)` needs 39 digits and, with `spark.sql.decimalOperations.allowPrecisionLoss` on (the default), keeps the scale up to `s = 6` and drops one digit past it, rounding half up: `0 - x` of a `DECIMAL(38,10)` is a `DECIMAL(38,9)` (spark-decimal-arith).
`Decimal.unary_-` negates the Scala `BigDecimal`, whose default `MathContext` is `DECIMAL128` (34 digits, `HALF_EVEN`); `Decimal.abs` calls it for a negative value only. Upstream bug SP-1.
reference: `negate` and `abs` of decimals are exact, and never overflow (the negation of a `DECIMAL(p,s)` fits it). Spark is wrong past 34 digits; a writer spells `-x` as `0 - x` and `abs(x)` as `CASE WHEN x < 0 THEN 0 - x ELSE x END`, exact for a scale up to 6; past it `0 - x` loses the last digit unless precision loss is off.

evidence.note: `unary_-`: `Decimal(-decimalVal, precision, scale)` on a Scala `BigDecimal`; `abs` calls it

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `unary_-` builds `-decimalVal` (a Scala `BigDecimal`, `MathContext.DECIMAL128`); `abs` is `if (this < Decimal.ZERO) this.unary_- else this`

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 7084 of 7084 results as the fact says; Spark's value differs from Rel.eval's (sverify's lift, reference profile) on 795 of 1111 rows compared.

notes: sverify_spark.dialect writes -x as 0 - x past 34 digits where its type keeps the scale (up to 37 digits, or 38 at scale 6 or less) and refuses DECIMAL(38, s) with s > 6; Spark.decimal_negate_sub (engines/spark/Sverify/Spark/Shims.lean). Spark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.13, macOS arm64, local[2].
